## Proof

**Setup and the renewal equation in transform form.**

Let $F^{*n}$ denote the $n$-fold convolution of $F$ with itself ($F^{*0}$ the unit mass at $0$). The renewal function is
$$m(t)=\mathbb{E}[N(t)]=\sum_{n\geq 1}F^{*n}(t).$$
Its Laplace–Stieltjes transform is
$$m^*(\theta)=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\theta t}\,dm(t)=\sum_{n\geq 1}\bigl(F^*(\theta)\bigr)^{n}=\frac{F^*(\theta)}{1-F^*(\theta)},$$
where $F^*(\theta)=\mathbb{E}[e^{-\theta X_1}]$ (the convention here is the Laplace transform; the stated "moment generating function" is used in this Laplace–Stieltjes sense, consistent with the limit $\theta\to 0$). The geometric series converges for $\theta>0$ since $|F^*(\theta)|<1$.

**Expansion of $F^*(\theta)$ near $\theta=0$.**

Since $\sigma^{2}<\infty$, the second moment $\mathbb{E}[X_1^{2}]=\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2}$ is finite, and Taylor expansion of $e^{-\theta x}$ (justified by dominated convergence, the remainder being $o(\theta^{2})$ under the finite second moment) gives
$$F^*(\theta)=1-\theta\,\mathbb{E}[X_1]+\frac{\theta^{2}}{2}\,\mathbb{E}[X_1^{2}]+o(\theta^{2})=1-\theta\mu+\frac{\theta^{2}}{2}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta^{2}).$$
Hence
$$1-F^*(\theta)=\theta\mu-\frac{\theta^{2}}{2}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta^{2})=\theta\mu\Bigl[1-\frac{\theta}{2\mu}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta)\Bigr].$$

**Form the ratio and expand.**

Using $F^*(\theta)=1-\theta\mu+\frac{\theta^{2}}{2}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta^{2})$ and the factorization above,
$$m^*(\theta)=\frac{F^*(\theta)}{1-F^*(\theta)}=\frac{1}{\theta\mu}\Bigl[1-\theta\mu+\tfrac{\theta^{2}}{2}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta^{2})\Bigr]\Bigl[1-\tfrac{\theta}{2\mu}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta)\Bigr]^{-1}.$$

Apply $(1-u)^{-1}=1+u+o(u)$ with $u=\frac{\theta}{2\mu}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})$:
$$\Bigl[1-\tfrac{\theta}{2\mu}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta)\Bigr]^{-1}=1+\frac{\theta}{2\mu}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})+o(\theta).$$

Multiplying the two brackets (keeping terms through $O(\theta)$, since the prefactor $1/(\theta\mu)$ promotes $O(\theta)$ to $O(1)$):
$$\Bigl[1-\theta\mu+\tfrac{\theta^{2}}{2}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})\Bigr]\Bigl[1+\tfrac{\theta}{2\mu}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})\Bigr]$$
$$=1+\frac{\theta}{2\mu}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})-\theta\mu+\underbrace{\frac{\theta^{2}}{2}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})-\frac{\theta^{2}}{2}(\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2})}_{=0}+o(\theta)$$
$$=1+\theta\Bigl[\frac{\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2}}{2\mu}-\mu\Bigr]+o(\theta)=1+\theta\,\frac{\sigma^{2}+\mu^{2}-2\mu^{2}}{2\mu}+o(\theta)=1+\theta\,\frac{\sigma^{2}-\mu^{2}}{2\mu}+o(\theta).$$

**Conclusion.**

Substituting back,
$$m^*(\theta)=\frac{1}{\theta\mu}\Bigl[1+\theta\,\frac{\sigma^{2}-\mu^{2}}{2\mu}+o(\theta)\Bigr]=\frac{1}{\theta\mu}+\frac{\sigma^{2}-\mu^{2}}{2\mu^{2}}+o(1)\quad\text{as }\theta\to 0.$$

This is the desired formal expansion. (The non-arithmetic assumption on $F$ guarantees the renewal theorem applies and that the constant term $\frac{\sigma^{2}-\mu^{2}}{2\mu^{2}}$ is well defined; the arithmetic case would introduce a lattice correction.) $\blacksquare$
